summary:
Beyond the Milkway is a browser-based space mission design game for 1–4 players. Its wording adapts to three age groups (5–12, 13–18, 19–60+), and it supports English, Malay and Mandarin. Players upgrade a spacecraft’s shield, heat protection, power and drive, choose a destination from the Moon to the Kuiper Belt, manage a limited budget, and decide how to react to random events such as solar flares. A zoomable orrery and a Sun-to-planet-to-moon scene graph show orbits, transfer paths and live numbers such as distance, delta-v and travel time, with an optional VR split view.

It addresses the challenge by letting players feel real engineering trade-offs: farther worlds need more delta-v and nuclear (RTG) power, hotter or more radioactive worlds need better protection, and every choice affects mission success. After each mission, a report explains why it succeeded or failed, names real NASA missions, and offers a GMAT-style script template.

It matters because it turns hard mission-design ideas into play, helping students and families understand how real missions are planned. It uses NASA’s Planetary Fact Sheet, real NASA mission examples and NASA Mission Viz concepts.
details:
WHAT IT DOES: Beyond the Milkway is a free, offline space-mission game for 1 to 4 players. Players upgrade a spacecraft, choose a destination from the Moon to the Kuiper Belt, pick a launch window, launch, and handle a random event as a team. A report explains why the mission succeeded or failed.

HOW IT WORKS: Fuel cost and travel time come from Hohmann-transfer maths and the NASA Planetary Fact Sheet. Off-window launches cost up to 60% more, and far planets need nuclear power because sunlight fades.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT: Players learn that every mission choice has a trade-off. Three age levels and three languages (English, Malay, Chinese) make it easy to understand for children and adults.

TOOLS: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Canvas API, Web Audio API, GMAT R2025a and NASA Mission Viz as references. Claude (an AI assistant) was used to check the code for errors, improve the layout and add the launch-window feature.

CREATIVITY AND FACTORS: Launch windows turn real orbital maths into a timing challenge. We considered different ages, small screens, offline use and teamwork.
